Lessons.Title: Multiplying Complex Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Calculate the result of multiplying two complex numbers. Justify that two equivalent expressions involving complex numbers are equivalent, using the fact that $i^2=\text-1$.

Source activity 13.1: $i$ Squared: Write each expression in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. \(4i \boldcdot 3i\) \(4i \boldcdot \text-3i\) \(\text- 2i \boldcdot \text- 5i\) \(\text- 5i \boldcdot 5i\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 13.2: Multiplying Imaginary Numbers: Take turns with your partner to match an expression in column A with an equivalent expression in column B. For each match that you find, explain to your partner how you know it’s a match. For each match that your partner finds, listen carefully to their explanation. If you disagree, discuss your thinking and work to reach an agreement. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 13.3: Multiplying Complex Numbers: Write each product in the form \(a + bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. \((\text- 3 + 9i)(5i)\) \((8 + i)(\text- 5 + 3i)\) \((3 + 2i)(3 - 2i)\) On October 16, 1843, while walking across the Broom Bridge in Dublin, Ireland, Sir William Rowan Hamilton came up with an idea for numbers that would work sort of like complex numbers. Practice Problem 1: Which expression is equivalent to \(2i(5+3i)\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Lin says, “When you add or multiply two complex numbers, you will always get an answer you can write in \(a + bi\) form.” Noah says, “I don’t think so. Here are some exceptions I found:” \((7 + 2i) + (3 - 2i) = 10\) \((2 + 2i)(2 + 2i) = 8i\) Check Noah’s arithmetic. Is it correct? Can Noah’s answers be written in the… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Explain to someone who missed class how you would write \((3-5i)(\text-2+4i)\) in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 4: Which expression is equal to \(729^{\frac23}\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Find the solution(s) to each equation, or explain why there is no solution. \(2x^2-\frac23= 5\frac13\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: Plot each number in the complex plane. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: Select all the expressions that are equivalent to \((3x+2)(x-4)\) for all real values of \(x\). \(3(x^2 + 2x - 4)\) \(3(x^2-3x)-(x+8)\) \(3x(x-3)-2(5x+4)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Multiply (1+2i)(1-2i). Expected reasoning or answer: 5.
